use_case_summary: Aurelia plans to deploy Redwood Private inside a customer-owned VPC to power contract review and automated redaction for enterprise law firms. Requirements: SSO via SAML 2.0, SCIM-based provisioning with group sync, strict RBAC in the Redwood control plane, BYOK KMS integration (AWS KMS primary), and audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance. Latency target: p50 < 120ms for short requests; peak batch throughput 300 QPS during nightly ingestion. Data residency: EU-only for specific clients but overall company HQ in NA; they require proof of per-customer residency segregation.
notes: CISO (Omar J.): 'We need assurance that customer CMKs are never available to Redwood staff and that any decryption requires the customer's key.'

Identity: Okta enterprise SSO. Expectation: SAML SP initiated login and SCIM v2 provisioning. They want group-to-role mapping: 'legal-admins' -> admin, 'ml-ops' -> se, 'reviewers' -> app-user, 'compliance' -> auditor-readonly.
SCIM pain: Okta sends group members as 'members' with value 'id' while our mapping doc expects 'value' attribute. SE to propose transformation layer or mapping template.
RBAC ask: console roles must be granular. Aurelia requires a custom role that can view logs and export them but cannot change KMS bindings.
KMS details: prefer AWS KMS key in Aurelia account with grant to Redwood control plane role. Needs example trust policy, key rotation cadence notes, and HSM-backed option details.

Audit logs: retention requested 5 years for admin actions and 2 years for access logs. Must support streaming to customer Splunk over HTTPS with signed delivery. Legal wants chain-of-custody for logs relevant to investigations.
Network: Private VPC peering to eu-west-1. Customer firewall must allow outbound to Redwood management IPs only. No public internet model payloads allowed. SE provided VPC template and CIDR ranges.
Compliance: Requested SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence and penetration test summary. Redwood to provide compliance packet and contact for penetration results.

POC steps agreed: 1) Exchange SAML metadata and validate SP initiated flow, 2) Configure SCIM group sync and provision 4 test users, 3) Attach customer CMK and perform encrypt/decrypt check, 4) Enable log forwarding and confirm log receipt in Splunk, 5) Run load test to validate latency SLOs.

Success metrics: SAML login success rate 100% for test users, SCIM create/deactivate within 60s, KMS-encrypted artifacts cannot be decrypted without customer key, logs appear in Splunk within 10s, p95 latency < 250ms under 300 QPS load.
